description: Common intermediate language, the CPU-independent instruction set the C# compiler emits into assemblies together with type metadata.
The compiled output of one project, usually a .dll, which holds CIL and metadata and is the boundary that the internal access modifier enforces.
The runtime compiles each method to native code on its first call, starting with quick code and recompiling hot methods with full optimization in the background.
The SDK builds apps (CLI, compiler, MSBuild, NuGet, templates) and includes a runtime, while a server only needs the runtime to execute a framework-dependent app.
A runtime component installed once per machine, such as Microsoft.NETCore.App or Microsoft.AspNetCore.App, that framework-dependent apps load at startup.
The default publish mode, which ships only your assemblies and relies on an installed runtime that rolls forward to the newest security patch.
A publish mode that compiles everything to native code ahead of time, trading runtime code generation and some ASP.NET Core features for faster startup and lower memory.
